title: Garner's Algorithm: Mixed-Radix CRT Reconstruction
description: Extends the two-modulus Bézout CRT solver (crtInt) to k pairwise-coprime moduli by formalizing Garner's algorithm — the classical mixed-radix reconstruction — and proving it returns the unique canonical CRT solution in [0, ∏ mᵢ).

meta.author: Lean Genius Research Agent (formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: Bézout's identity for integers: gcd(a,b) = a * gcdA + b * gcdB — the cofactor gcdA P m is used as the modular inverse of P modulo m
First Bézout coefficient for integers, reused as the running modular inverse in each Garner digit
Integer modular congruence iff divisibility: a ≡ b [ZMOD n] ↔ n ∣ b - a
Bounds 0 ≤ x % m < m for m > 0, giving the genuine mixed-radix digit range
Coprime divisors multiply: lifts each modulus dividing (garner − y) to their product dividing it, driving uniqueness
Coprimality distributes over products, used to maintain coprimality of the running partial product against the remaining moduli

originalContributions: First formalization of Garner's mixed-radix CRT reconstruction over ℤ as a single left-to-right sweep (garnerAux) carrying only the running value and partial product
Realizes the per-step modular inverse without any ZMod.inv plumbing — the Bézout cofactor Int.gcdA P m already inverts P mod m, the very identity behind the parent crtInt
garner_modEq: every system congruence is satisfied, proved via a preservation lemma (garnerAux_modEq_self) showing the sweep never disturbs already-accumulated residues
garner_range: the genuine mixed-radix bound 0 ≤ x < ∏ mᵢ, the defining feature distinguishing Garner's form from a raw CRT sum
garner_unique: Garner returns THE canonical CRT solution, via list-prod coprimality (isCoprime_list_prod_right) and IsCoprime.mul_dvd
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Built entirely on Mathlib's Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab (Bézout) and IsCoprime.mul_dvd; only Lean's foundational axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

overview.historicalContext: The two-modulus Chinese Remainder Theorem reconstructs a residue from a pair of coprime moduli; for k moduli the naive approach computes one large modular inverse against the full product. **Garner's algorithm** (Harvey L. Garner, *The residue number system*, 1959) instead builds the answer in **mixed-radix** form by a single left-to-right sweep, carrying only the running value and a running partial product. It is the workhorse behind residue number system (RNS) arithmetic and big-integer CRT reconstruction. This entry extends the gallery's integer-native two-modulus solver `crtInt` (bezout-identity-oq-03) to arbitrarily many pairwise-coprime moduli, proving the sweep both correct and canonical.
overview.keyInsight: Garner's per-step modular inverse needs no dedicated inversion machinery: the Bézout cofactor `Int.gcdA P m` already satisfies `P · gcdA P m ≡ 1 [ZMOD m]` whenever `m` is coprime to the partial product `P`. This is exactly the identity that powers `crtInt`, so the multi-modulus algorithm reuses the parent's single arithmetic fact. The `% m` reduction of each digit is what keeps the running value bounded in `[0, ∏ mᵢ)` — the defining feature of *Garner's* mixed-radix form.
overview.approach: Define the Garner `digit`, the sweep accumulator `garnerAux` (carrying value `x` and partial product `P`), and the public `garner` (sweeping from `(0,1)`). Prove three results: (1) `garner_modEq` — correctness against every congruence, leaning on a preservation lemma that the sweep never disturbs earlier residues; (2) `garner_range` — the mixed-radix bound `0 ≤ x < ∏ mᵢ`; (3) `garner_unique` — any representative in range satisfying all congruences equals `garner`, via pairwise-coprimality lifting divisibility to the product.

sections.title: Imports
sections.summary: Imports the full Mathlib for Bézout coefficients (Int.gcdA), integer modular congruence (Int.ModEq), and coprimality lemmas (IsCoprime.mul_dvd).
sections.mathContext: The single arithmetic ingredient is `Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab : (Int.gcd a b : ℤ) = a * Int.gcdA a b + b * Int.gcdB a b`, Mathlib's formalized Bézout identity.

sections.title: Module Documentation
sections.summary: States the open question (extend crtInt to k moduli), describes Garner's mixed-radix sweep, the per-step digit formula, and why the Bézout cofactor serves as the modular inverse.
sections.mathContext: Garner builds x = v₁ + v₂·m₁ + v₃·m₁m₂ + ⋯ + v_k·m₁⋯m_{k-1} with digit vⱼ = (rⱼ − x)·(P⁻¹ mod mⱼ) reduced into [0, mⱼ), where P = m₁⋯m_{j-1}.

sections.title: Garner Digit and Sweep
sections.summary: `digit` computes (r − x)·(gcdA P m) % m; `garnerAux` carries (x, P) left-to-right across the (modulus, residue) list; `garner` sweeps from (0, 1).
sections.mathContext: The accumulator update is x ← x + digit·P, P ← P·m. Carrying only x and P makes the sweep a single linear pass with no precomputed product-inverses.

sections.title: Digit Facts
sections.summary: digit_nonneg and digit_lt give 0 ≤ digit < m (from Int.emod bounds); digit_modEq relates the reduced digit to its un-reduced Bézout form mod m.
sections.mathContext: 0 ≤ x % m < m for m > 0 is what bounds every mixed-radix digit; digit ≡ (r − x)·gcdA P m [ZMOD m] lets the % m reduction drop out of all congruence reasoning.

sections.title: Running Product
sections.summary: garnerAux_snd: after the sweep the second component equals the starting P times the product of all moduli — pinning the mixed-radix modulus to ∏ mᵢ.
sections.mathContext: (garnerAux x P pairs).2 = P · ∏ (pairs.map fst). Starting from P = 1 this is exactly the CRT modulus ∏ mᵢ.

sections.title: Modular Inverse from Bézout
sections.summary: gcdA_mul_modEq_one: the Bézout cofactor inverts P modulo any coprime m. isCoprime_list_prod_right: coprimality distributes over a list product.
sections.mathContext: From gcd(P,m)=1 and 1 = P·gcdA + m·gcdB we get P·gcdA ≡ 1 [ZMOD m]. This is the single arithmetic fact reused from crtInt — no ZMod.inv needed.

sections.title: Residue Preservation
sections.summary: garnerAux_modEq_self: after processing the remaining pairs from (x, P), the result is still ≡ x [ZMOD P]. This protects the residues of all earlier moduli (each divides P).
sections.mathContext: Each subsequent increment is a multiple of the current P, so the running value stays fixed modulo P — the invariant that keeps already-solved congruences solved.

sections.title: Correctness of Every Congruence
sections.summary: garnerAux_modEq: the swept value satisfies p.2 ≡ value [ZMOD p.1] for every pair. The head step uses the Bézout inverse; the tail uses preservation + induction.
sections.mathContext: Head: x + digit·P ≡ r [ZMOD m] because digit·P ≡ (r − x)·(P·gcdA) ≡ (r − x) [ZMOD m]. Tail residues survive by garnerAux_modEq_self applied at modulus m ∣ P·m.

sections.title: Mixed-Radix Range
sections.summary: garnerAux_range: 0 ≤ value < running product, by induction maintaining 0 ≤ x < P and using 0 ≤ digit < m with x + digit·P < P·m.
sections.mathContext: The bound x + (m−1)·P + P = P·m shows each step's value stays below the new product P·m — the genuine mixed-radix bound 0 ≤ x < ∏ mᵢ.

sections.title: Public Interface
sections.summary: garner_modEq (solves every congruence), garner_range (canonical representative in [0, ∏ mᵢ)), and garner_unique (any in-range solution equals garner) — Garner returns THE CRT solution.
sections.mathContext: Uniqueness: each mᵢ divides garner − y; pairwise coprimality lifts this (isCoprime_list_prod_right + IsCoprime.mul_dvd) to ∏ mᵢ ∣ garner − y, and two representatives in [0, ∏) forced equal by |c| < 1.

conclusion.summary: This formalization extends the gallery's two-modulus Bézout CRT solver to k pairwise-coprime moduli via Garner's mixed-radix algorithm, fully machine-checked at 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The key economy is that the per-step modular inverse is the Bézout cofactor Int.gcdA — the same single arithmetic fact behind crtInt — so the multi-modulus reconstruction needs no new inversion machinery. The three headline results establish that the single left-to-right sweep is correct (solves every congruence), bounded (genuine mixed-radix range), and canonical (returns the unique CRT solution).
conclusion.futureWork: Specialize garner to concrete RNS bases and prove an efficiency/bit-bound; relate garner to Mathlib's ZMod.chineseRemainder; extend to the non-coprime case by pre-reducing to coprime prime-power moduli.
